doc_friction.issue: Step 0 says fix every open defect first, but all 11 open entries are control-plane edits (workflows, prompts/, platform/ci guard) needing their own owner-approved PRs, so step 0 is a no-op for an ordinary run; the list only grows.

deviations.why: Step 0: the 11 open defects all need control-plane PRs that wait for owner approval; several already have patches or PRs waiting.
deviations.did: Left them as they were and spent the run on a new target.
deviations.result: Two new real defects found and patched in rev-rec.

deviations.why: Step 4b (an automated guard for the class): the five sibling money parsers that strip commas belong to US-only tools (Schedule C, US contractors, US banks), so a lint for decimal-comma handling would flag correct code.
deviations.did: Listed the siblings in notes and in the post instead of adding a lint.
deviations.result: No new CI guard this run.

notes: Targets: ventures/rev-rec revrec.mjs (9/10), stripe.mjs (7/10), csv.mjs (4/10); after the new tests all 9 gaps were caught (rerun), so the catch rate went from 0.69 to 1.0. Real defects: decimal-comma amounts read 100x too large (csv.mjs parseAmount), and the browser demo summed mixed currencies (oneCurrency, checked in Chromium with Playwright). Unverified lead for a later run: stripe.mjs reads t.inclusive on tax_amounts/taxes, but newer Stripe API versions may give line 'taxes' a tax_behavior field instead of inclusive; check against the current API docs. Siblings parsing money by stripping commas (US-only, left as they are): expense-tracker/calc.mjs toCents, bid-leveling-worksheet/calc.mjs parseMoney, contractor-wip-schedule/calc.mjs moneyNum, ai-bookkeeper/bank.mjs:1334, ai-bookkeeper/receipts.mjs:88. Local checks: rev-rec node --test 49/49; run_workflow_locally --for-changes: portfolio-validate 99/99, ventures-tests 5/5, pages 6/6, link/doc/page checks green; prompts-ci failed only on this record's unfilled outcome before it was filled in (re-run below).

real_defects.issue: A decimal-comma amount (European export) was read 100x too large or garbled: "29,00" became 2,900.00 and "1.234,50" became 1.23, with no row skipped. Reproduced with linesFromCsv; fixed with parseAmount (a comma before one or two final digits is a decimal comma) and a failing-first test.

The browser demo summed lines in different currencies into one schedule labelled with the first line's currency (the server already keeps one currency). Fixed with oneCurrency() in csv.mjs (keep the most common currency, report the rest in the message) and a failing-first test; checked in Chromium.

pricing.source: Anthropic pricing as cached in the Claude API skill (models table and per-model migration notes), 2026-10-06. Cache writes are 1.25x input (5-minute) and 2x input (1-hour); cache reads differ by model.

human_equivalent.basis: triage of 30 mutants, two bug fixes with tests, browser check, post

certainty.tokens: high: summed from the per-request `usage` the API returned, as the transcript recorded it, deduplicated by message id
certainty.model: high: the `model` field on each API response, not the configured model
certainty.api_equivalent_usd: medium: measured tokens x list prices in prompts/pricing.json (as_of stated); an equivalent, not a charge: these runs are billed under a subscription
certainty.time: medium: from transcript timestamps; model time is request-to-response, tool time is call-to-result, time waiting on a person is excluded from active time
certainty.human_equivalent: low: the agent's own estimate of how long a competent person would take, with its basis written down; never measured

not_counted: requests the harness makes outside the transcript (context compaction summaries, title generation, safety classifiers), if any
transcripts lost when a cloud session moved to a new container: only files present in this container are read, so a resumed session can undercount
server-tool fees (web search is billed per search, not per token); the count is recorded, not priced
